key_insight: The researchers introduce EVA, a long-context RNA foundation model that predicts RNA function and generates RNA designs. The study investigates RNA scaling laws and supports the model’s capabilities with experimental validation.
problem_solved: RNA design requires models that can handle long sequences while connecting sequence information to biological function across different design tasks.
method: Investigate scaling laws for RNA modeling to inform foundation-model development.
Develop EVA as a long-context generative model for RNA function prediction and diverse RNA design.
Experimentally validate model capabilities and RNA designs.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, EVA illustrates how long-context generative modeling can support both prediction and design in biology. The experimental validation connects computational modeling with biological testing.
visual_elements: A long RNA sequence feeding into EVA, with outputs branching into function prediction and RNA design.
A conceptual scaling-law chart showing model scale versus performance, clearly labeled as illustrative.
An RNA sequence-to-structure diagram highlighting interactions between distant sequence regions.
A workflow linking generated RNA candidates to laboratory validation.
paper_title: A long-context generative foundation model for versatile RNA design
paper_authors: Yanjie Huang, Guangye Lv, Ziheng Gao, Anyue Cheng, Wei Xie
